{{Quote|Without the midi-chlorians, life could not exist, and we would have no knowledge of the Force. They continually speak to us, telling us the will of the Force. When you learn to quiet your mind, you'll hear them speaking to you.|Qui-Gon Jinn, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
'''Midi-chlorians''' were [[Sentience/Legends|intelligent]] microscopic life-forms that lived symbiotically inside the cells of all living things. When present in sufficient numbers, they could allow their host to detect the pervasive energy field known as [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Midi-chlorian counts were linked to potential in the Force, ranging from normal [[Human/Legends|Human]] levels of 2,500 per cell to the much higher levels of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. The highest known midi-chlorian count&mdash;over 20,000 per cell&mdash;belonged to the Jedi [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who was believed to have been [[Reproduction/Legends|conceived]] by the midi-chlorians.<ref name="Star Wars: Graphics">According to the chart in ''[[Star Wars: Graphics]]'' (pages 50-51), some humans, such as [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]], had lower levels of 1,500 per cell, while Anakin's count is stated to be 27,700. According to the chart key, the minimum count needed for a person to become a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi]] was 7,000, with an average count for a Jedi of 10,000.</ref>

Midi-chlorian counts were measured through a [[Blood/Legends|blood]] test; the Jedi used this method to locate [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] children before their [[Jedi Order/Legends|Order]] was [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|purged]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. With the rise of the Empire, research into Jedi and the Force was banned, and though midi-chlorians continued to be tested for, sometimes by the Empire itself to root out hidden Jedi and other Force-sensitives, knowledge of them was diminished and inquiries into them were branded as illegal medical research. Midi-chlorians were only rediscovered after the [[New Jedi Order]] was founded.

When not forbidden, studies of midi-chlorians occurred among both those who could master the Force and those who could not. While medical teams worked to understand the relationship between midi-chlorians and the Force, [[Jedi healer/Legends|Jedi healers]] performed their own studies of the organisms. Even more esoteric studies were conducted by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], who discovered a way to [[Midi-chlorian manipulation|manipulate the midi-chlorians to create new life]].

==Biology==
{{Quote|They live inside me?|Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="TPM" />}}
Midi-chlorians were [[Sentience/Legends|intelligent]]<ref name="TPMn" /> microscopic lifeforms that served as organelles within all living cells, existing in a symbiotic relationship with the beings they inhabited<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="MS">''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]''</ref> and comprising a collective consciousness among themselves.<ref name="TPMn" /> Present in all life,<ref name="NEGAS" /> midi-chlorians were isomorphic on every [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that supported life.<ref name="MS" /> Midi-chlorians, in fact, were necessary for life to exist. They also allowed for a connection with the pervasive energy field known as [[The Force/Legends|the Force]];<ref name="TPM" /> in sufficient numbers, midi-chlorians could allow their symbiont organism to detect the Force, and this connection could be strengthened by quieting one's mind,<ref name="NEGAS" /> allowing the midi-chlorians to "speak" to their symbiont and communicate the will of the Force.<ref name="TPM" /> Counts as low as 2,000 midi-chlorians per cell provided no sensitivity to the Force;<ref name="SOS">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> an average [[Human/Legends|Human]] had less than 2,500 per cell, while a mildly [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] being such as [[Nova Stihl]] had a count in excess of 5,000.<ref name="DS">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> According to [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]], a being born of "pure force" might have a count of 15,000 or more, implying that most Force-sensitives did not have a count that high.<ref name="The Tenebrous Way">{{InsiderCite|130|The Tenebrous Way}}</ref> [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] had especially high midi-chlorian counts, and of them [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was said to have the highest ever recorded<ref name="NEGAS" /> at over 20,000, even higher than the powerful [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]].<ref name="TPM" /> Though Skywalker later lost a good deal of his organic body, his cells continued to teem with midi-chlorians.<ref name="BP">''[[Star Wars Blueprints: The Ultimate Collection]]''</ref> Moreover, he could overcome any apparent loss of Force ability, (with the exception of being unable to use Force Lightning or other powers that had to be cast through living cells), if he was to overcome his mental limitations.<ref name=":0">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

[[File:Anakins_lightsaber.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Anakin Skywalker, a being possibly conceived by the midi-chlorians]]
The magnitude of the midi-chlorian count served as a measure of one's potential in the Force,<ref name="EGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> though there were other inheritable characteristics that could influence Force ability as well.<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> Indeed, though Force ability often meant a high midi-chlorian count, it was not always the case.<ref name="Jedi Order">{{DB|organization|thejediorder|Jedi Order, The}}</ref> While some medical theories postulated that the midi-chlorians created the connection between more macroscopic organisms and the Force, some Jedi believed that, contrarily, the midi-chlorians were created by the Force to serve as the link between it and other life.<ref name="MS" /> Midi-chlorian counts did not indicate an upper limit to Force ability; the possibility existed for a Jedi to achieve a connection to the Force on an equivalent level to a Jedi with a higher count.<ref name="TPMn" /> Moreover, and in spite of the misconception to the contrary<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref>, a being that lost one or more limbs was not necessarily reduced in the Force—any such reduction in power owed to the mental failings of the wounded Force Sensitive which could be overcome with willpower,<ref name=":0" /> not to a loss of their potential.<ref name="Darth P" /> The sole exception were Force powers like [[Force lightning/Legends|Lightning]] that had to be channeled though living flesh—and even then only the possible points of origin were restricted.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Darth P" /><ref name="Book of Sith" />

Midi-chlorians could be influenced by the Force to create new life, a technique developed by [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> There was even a possibility that they could induce conception in a Human; Anakin Skywalker was believed to have been conceived by the midi-chlorians, with no biological father.<ref name="NEGAS" /> This was considered impossible by many Jedi, however, and the idea received only shock when it was first proposed to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]].<ref name="TPMn" />
[[File:Grievous_tank.jpg|thumb|Grievous was infused with the Sifo-Dyas's blood, but did not receive the Jedi's Force-sensitivity.]]
Though tested for, midi-chlorians did not usually figure into the medical treatment of most beings, and they were linked to no known pathology.<ref name="DS" /> Chemicals used in medicine, such as anesthetics, could thin the midi-chlorians; if it was vital they be preserved, a being could be operated on without anesthesia.<ref name="RAF">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref> The drug [[Bota/Legends|bota]], on the other hand, was thought capable of boosting the effects of the midi-chlorians, enhancing an individual's Force-sensitivity.<ref name="SOS" /> An organism that had been grievously injured and unable to be kept alive through medical treatment could be infused with [[Blood/Legends|blood]] rich in midi-chlorians, forcing an organism to stay alive when it would normally [[Death/Legends|die]], as was the case with [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]. However, this would not transfer any of the blood donor's Force-sensitivity.<ref name="Grievous">{{InsiderCite|86|Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous}}</ref>

The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] virus known as [[Imperial bioweapons Project I71A|the Sickness]] could alter the midi-chlorians within an infected individual. The Sith Lord [[Darth Drear]] devised it as a means of immortality, the final step of which involved eating the living heart of a Jedi, and thus obtaining an infusion of midi-chlorians from the Jedi's blood. He was never able to capture a Jedi with sufficiently high midi-chlorian count before dying, however.<ref name="RH">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref>

When [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Tenebrous was killed by his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] Plagueis on [[Bal'demnic/Legends|Bal'demnic]], amidst the billions upon billions of individual midi-chlorians in his cells, a tiny fraction of his midi-chlorians were not dying. They would not die as long as they inhabited a living host. These especially tenacious midi-chlorians were privately named [[maxi-chlorian]]s by Tenebrous himself, and had been altered to be long-lived midi-chlorians, and would migrate, not in the Force, but into Plagueis, as a retrovirus designed to infect the host's blood, in order to gain conscience beyond death.<ref name="The Tenebrous Way" /> At the same time, Darth Plagueis sensed Tenebrous' midi-chlorians wink out, like lights slowly deprived of a power source, and yet, he could perceive his master in the Force.<ref name="Darth P">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

Plagueis' work with midi-chlorians was directly rooted in what was traditionally considered the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]], or those energies attached to the anima and the pneuma. At the same time, Plagueis mused that although the [[Unifying Force/Legends|Unifying Force]] was not specifically necessary for the creation and manipulation of life, midi-chlorians channeled it nonetheless. Through his studies, Plagueis found that the aperion governs the cohesion of matter, from the atoms of a pebble to all planets and [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] in the universe, including the dimension of [[Time/Legends|time]], which could be possibly manipulated on a grand scale, allowing an individual to step instantly from one place to another by folding space, regardless of the intervening distance. The anima governs life, and it is through this state that all [[Force healing/Legends|Force healing]] is possible. The pneuma governs consciousness, and through this, Plagueis was convinced that the energy pattern known as self-awareness could be preserved and imprinted a second time into the neural pathways of a different [[Brain/Legends|brain]].<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Force-sensitive members of the rock-based [[B'rknaa]] [[Species/Legends|species]] had microscopic midi-chlorian-infused structures that were very different from the midi-chlorian-infused cells of organic beings.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

Though rumored, the [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]] were resistant to Force suggestion. The species has a survival mechanism, in which the midi-chlorians protected the consciousness of their vessels by refusing to be manipulated. Despite this, Plagueis had managed to lower down that defence and use Force suggestion on a captured Yinchorr.<ref name="Darth P" />

==Study and analysis==
{{Quote|Target midi-chlorians and we target life itself.|Darth Plagueis to Darth Sidious|<ref name="Darth P" />}}
[[File:Blood_sample.png|thumb|right|250px|Qui-Gon Jinn taking a blood sample from Anakin Skywalker for midi-chlorian analysis.]]
Midi-chlorians could be detected through a blood test by measuring their concentration in a being's red blood cells,<ref name="BP" /> though such tests were not perfect and were prone to fault.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Midi-chlorian tests were part of a standard medical check-up, recorded in a blood analysis.<ref name="DS" /> From at least [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], blood tests for midi-chlorians were the primary way by which the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] found Force-sensitive children.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Such tests were mandatory for beings born in regions controlled by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TJP" /> Some Jedi comlinks could have midi-chlorian samplers attached to them to measure blood samples,<ref name="Comlink">{{DB|technology|comlink|comlink}}</ref> though these results would need to be interpolated through a computer, such as that found aboard a [[Starship/Legends|starship]], to get a count.<ref name="TPM" /> Darth Vader had an entire blood-testing system in his [[Darth Vader's meditation chamber/Legends|meditation chamber]], which he not only used to test for infections, but also measure his midi-chlorian count.<ref name="BP" />

While most research on midi-chlorians was conducted by [[Jedi healer/Legends|Jedi healers]],<ref name="DS" /> the connection between midi-chlorians and the Force was studied in non-Jedi medical circles as well, with theories advanced as to the relation between them.<ref name="MS" /> On [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]], high midi-chlorian counts were a mark of status, possessed by the more prestigious families. As a result, interest in the midi-chlorians remained high on that world.<ref name="DR">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref>

Experimentation on midi-chlorians happened occasionally as well. Nobles on Vjun conducted forbidden<ref name="Vjun">{{DB|location|vjun|Vjun}}</ref> experiments on the life-forms in an attempt to increase Force sensitivity, the results of which drove the population of Vjun insane.<ref name="DR" /> Darth Plagueis, Dark Lord of the Sith, sought a way of influencing the midi-chlorians with the Force to create new life from nothing, and he may have succeeded before his death at the hands of his apprentice.<ref name="Vader">''[[Vader: The Ultimate Guide]]''</ref> Plagueis also possessed a lab located in the planet [[Aborah]], in which he experimented with different species, altering their midi-chlorians in order to prolong their lives. Some time later, after killing Darth Tenebrous, [[Darth Venamis]] sought to get revenge on Plagueis. However, Venamis was defeated and kept by Plagueis in his lab in a near-coma stasis. Through the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Plagueis experimented with Venamis, killing and reviving him, manipulating the midi-chlorians within the [[Bith/Legends|Bith's]] body.<ref name="Darth P" /> Therefore, Plagueis concluded that in order to stop aging, the solution was not to add more midi-chlorians to a body, but to impose one's will on the midi-chlorians already present on the subject; because midi-chlorians were linked by a universal mind, the ones in Plagueis' cells initially resisted his imposition upon their fellows, but eventually he succeeded, first with small creatures, then with [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]. Through these experiments, Plagueis discovered that these midi-chlorians would not die; instead, they drew upon sustaining Force energy, which acted on a microscopic level to halt tissue decay in their host, putting an end to aging and disease. In his writings, Plagueis believed this could only be achieved with a sharpened mental focus and an affinity for the Force to impose a measurable effect on living cells.<ref name="Book of Sith" /> [[Darth Drear]], another Sith Lord, incorporated the midi-chlorians into his own research into immortality.<ref name="RH" />

The [[Force detector]] was one of the tools developed to measure midi-chlorian counts. Based on plans of the [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Jenna Zan Arbor]], the Force Detector consisted of a pair of paddles connected to a control pack; the paddles were placed around the subject, at which point the control pack would read out a list of statistics, including midi-chlorian count. It also generated a blue nimbus around a wireframe [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of the subject; though this correlated to Force-sensitivity, it was not a direct measurement of the subject's midi-chlorian concentration.<ref name="DTF">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/81/indexp7.html|text=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena|int=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)}}</ref> The [[DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid/Legends|DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid]], a tool of the Sith, was also capable of scanning lifeforms for the presence of midi-chlorians.<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

Measuring midi-chlorian counts was not always accurate, particularly among older children or individuals with unusual psychologies. The Jedi therefore sometimes used alternative methods to determine Force-sensitivity, such as testing with a [[mental maze]] or [[Jedi testing screen/Legends|testing screen]].<ref name="TJP" />

==History==
{{Quote|Frankly, the entire concept of midi-chlorians is unclear to us.|[[Wil Jhonems]], marketing manager for the Spotts Tradechip Company|<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|jediwatch/1344_2.html|Jedi TradeChips Spark Controversy}}</ref>}}
===Early years===
[[File:Midi-chlorian_homeworld.png|thumb|right|250px|The planet where midi-chlorians evolved as it looked by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].]]
Midi-chlorians evolved on a [[Wellspring of Life/Legends|luminous planet]] located somewhere "in the heart of the galaxy", according to the [[Force Priestesses/Legends|Five Priestesses]].<ref name="Destiny" /><ref name="Insider148" />

Before the creation of the Jedi Order around [[25,783 BBY]], a number of Force sects including the [[Followers of Palawa]], [[Chatos Academy]], and [[Order of Dai Bendu]] studied the Force scientifically, including the science of midi-chlorians, on worlds from [[Had Abbadon]] to [[Ondos]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The Sith knew of midi-chlorians by c. [[4645 BBY]], when Darth Drear utilized them in his experiments on immortality.<ref name="RH" /> Circa [[3956 BBY]], the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], a species that had almost lost all trace of Force-sensitivity, conducted their own scientific inquiries to find a genetic basis for the Force, which they hoped would allow them to become Force-sensitive once again.<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> How the Jedi detected Force-sensitives in their early millennia was lost to time, but shortly after the [[Ruusan campaign|Battle of Ruusan]] in 1000 BBY, midi-chlorians were either discovered by them for the first time, or rediscovered after having lost knowledge of them in an earlier era<ref name="EGTTF" />&mdash;at least one Jedi, [[Hestizo Trace]], had known of the existence of midi-chlorians as early as [[3645 BBY]].<ref name="RH" /> Blood tests for midi-chlorians were instituted to find recruits with a connection to the Force, a method used by the Jedi for almost a thousand years until the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|purge of the Jedi]] in 19 BBY.<ref name="EGTTF" /> In an event that would have repercussions a very long time in the future, a prophecy was made in these early days of a [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]] who would bring balance to the Force and was said to have a high concentration of midi-chlorians.<ref name="TPMn" />

On the world of Vjun, a high midi-chlorian count was synonymous with status, leading to a surge of interest in midi-chlorian phenomena. When Vjun came into contact with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and Jedi Order, the most eminent families&mdash;those with the highest counts&mdash;sought to protect themselves from Jedi recruitment by augmenting their own abilities. The seventeenth [[Viscount (title)/Legends|Viscount]] [[Malreaux]] of the esteemed [[House Malreaux]], along with a consortium of others, worked to genetically manipulate the midi-chlorians and thereby enhance the counts of Vjun's population. They were successful, but at a cost: when the entire planet became Force-sensitive with no mental training to handle it, the populace went mad and murdered each other.<ref name="DR" />

[[File:Plagueis_head.jpg|thumb|left|Darth Plagueis, manipulator of the midi-chlorians]]
In the decades before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Plagueis commenced his own experiments with the midi-chlorians. While the Jedi thought of the cellular organelles as symbionts, Plagueis believed they were interlopers, running interference for the Force, and standing in the way of a beings' ability to contact the Force directly. Through years of experimentation, Plagueis had honed an ability to perceive the actions of midi-chlorians. Furthermore, Plagueis believed that only the Sith understood that sentient life was on the verge of a transformative leap; that through the manipulation of midi-chlorians, or the overthrow of the Forceful group that supervised them, the divide between organic life and the Force could be bridged, and death could be erased from the continuum. In order to further the [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]], Darth Plagueis, and his apprentice, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], committed an act in direct violation to the nature of the Force, and attempted to tip its balance toward the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. The experiment yielded unfruitful however, and the midi-chlorians, unwilling to comply, struck back in retaliation conceiving a savior to ultimately destroy the Sith: the prophesied [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]], Anakin Skywalker.<ref name="Darth P" />

[[File:Midi_Count.jpg|thumb|right|A computer readout of Anakin Skywalker's midi-chlorian count]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] was stranded on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he encountered the slave boy Anakin Skywalker. Jinn sensed the Force strongly in Skywalker, and when he learned from the boy's mother [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]] that Anakin had had no father, Jinn realized that there was something special about him. That night, Jinn took a blood sample from a scrape on Skywalker's arm and tested it, telling the boy that he was checking for infections. Jinn had his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] run a midi-chlorian test on the sample; Kenobi was surprised to find Skywalker's count was off the chart&mdash;over 20,000. This exceeded that of even the powerful Master Yoda, or any other Jedi. Jinn later brought Skywalker to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and took him before the Jedi Council. There he informed them of Skywalker's unusually high midi-chlorian count and stated his belief that the boy had been conceived by the midi-chlorians. Jinn was referring to the prophecy of the Chosen One; while the Council recognized the reference, they did not agree with Jinn's conclusion,<ref name="TPM" /> although some Jedi nonetheless believed Skywalker had the potential to become the most powerful Jedi ever.<ref name="RAF" /> The lore of the Sith Lords claimed that Skywalker's conception had been a result of Plagueis' manipulations of the midi-chlorians.<ref name="Vader" />

By these latter years of the Republic, midi-chlorians were a matter of public knowledge, though some found the idea of them to be unclear. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Spotts TradeChip Company]] released a set of [[tradechip]]s of famous [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], featuring data, including midi-chlorian counts, garnered from what the company called the "best information available." However, the chips attracted criticism from the Jedi Order for their inaccuracies, as did the midi-chlorian counts provided; Yoda's, for example, provided the wildly inaccurate number of four million. Spotts defended its product, claiming that all mistakes were minor.<ref name="HNN" />

Later that year, [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], leader of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] movement, revealed to the Jedi that Plagueis' apprentice Darth Sidious secretly controlled the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Seventeen months later, the Jedi [[Ronhar Kim]] conceived of the idea to test the midi-chlorian counts of the [[Senator/Legends|senators]], believing that the Force-sensitive Sith would be revealed in this way. Kim approached [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine with his plan, but Palpatine, who secretly was Sidious, discouraged him, advising him that it would be politically impossible. Upon learning that Kim had not spoken of his idea to the Jedi Council, Palpatine arranged for the Jedi to be killed in a trap, and Kim's plan was never implemented.<ref name="R64">[[Republic 64|''Republic'' 64]]</ref>

===Under the Empire===
[[File:ForceDetector.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Force Detectors, a tool used to measure midi-chlorian counts]]
In the closing years of the Republic, studies of midi-chlorians were conducted by Jedi healers and medical personnel alike.<ref name="MS" /><ref name="DS" /> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] defector [[Ko Sai/Legends|Ko Sai]] was one of the scientists who sought to uncover the mysteries of the midi-chlorians and Jedi genome.<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref> The Jedi Order in its later years established a taboo over empirical studies into the Force and its tangible aspects, believing it could not be scientifically studied. When the Order was disbanded and Galactic Empire [[Declaration of a New Order|declared]], though, the taboo was broken. The scientists of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine treated the Force as a purely physical phenomenon, breaking it apart into the tangible components of midi-chlorians and energy. The [[Force detector|Force Detector]] and [[Force-detecting chip]] was one of the results of these studies, and it was used by the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]] in the Great Jedi Purge.<ref name="DTF" /> During the reign of the Empire, midi-chlorian tests were performed routinely on [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner]] and [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] worlds to root out Force-sensitives and Jedi in hiding. Such individuals were rarely heard from again. In response, an underground trade of drugs and blood treatments sprang up that could supposedly fool a test or lower one's count; however, they were largely ineffective.<ref name="NEGAS" />

After the rise of the Empire, Palpatine ordered a complete ban on all information related to Jedi or the Force and had such data purged from data banks galaxy-wide. [[Statute OB-CPO-1198]], covering illegal medical research that included studies of midi-chlorians, was also enacted. With the Jedi's records on midi-chlorians no longer available for study and any information on their relation to the Force kept out of medical libraries, medical professionals knew little of the nature of midi-chlorians, even as they continued to test for them. When [[Kornell Divini]], a [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], measured an abnormally high midi-chlorian count from one of his patients, he put out a request on the [[MedNet]] for any further information on midi-chlorians. Divini's search triggered warning flags put in place by the Empire, attracting the attention of the Emperor's servant Darth Vader, and Divini was arrested under the provisions of OB-CPO-1198.<ref name="DS" />

At a top-secret facility on the [[Frozen moon]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], Imperial scientists under [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] collected [[DNA/Legends|DNA]] from multiple Force-sensitives and cloned them, altering the midi-chlorians in their blood.<ref name="Riptide">[[Riptide (novel)|''Riptide'']]</ref>

When [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] established his [[New Jedi Order]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], he had no knowledge of midi-chlorian tests and as a result was forced to devise his own tests for finding Force-sensitives. The midi-chlorian method was rediscovered by the Order at some point before [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]].<ref name="EGTTF" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Origins===
{{Quote|It is said that certain creatures are born with a higher awareness of the Force than humans. Their brains are different.|George Lucas, establishing guidelines for the Expanded Universe in 1977|<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'', hardcover edition</ref>}}
Midi-chlorians were first conceived by [[George Lucas]] as early as [[1977]]. In this time the first [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] products were being created, including the ongoing [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel Star Wars]] series and [[Alan Dean Foster]]'s novel ''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''. Lucas sat down with a member of his staff, [[Carol Titelman]], to dictate a number of guidelines for these works, explaining various concepts of his universe. Among them were an explanation of midi-chlorians, which Force-sensitive beings were said to have more of in their cells.<ref name="Making" /> However, Lucas did not feel he had the time to introduce the concept of midi-chlorians. The idea would not appear in any ''[[Star Wars]]'' product for twenty-two years; Lucas chose [[1999]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] as the opportunity to first mention the midi-chlorians, explaining why some were sensitive to the Force while others were not, an issue that he had left unresolved since the original film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']]. Lucas incorporated the explanation of midi-chlorians into the film as part of Anakin Skywalker's journey towards understanding the Force.<ref name="TPM DVD">{{Film|I}} DVD commentary</ref> That Lucas had planned the midi-chlorians as far back as 1977 was hinted at on the DVD commentary of ''The Phantom Menace'', but the details would not be fully revealed for another eight years, coming to light in the [[2007]] book ''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'', the hardcover edition of which had, among its appendices, Lucas' notes for the Expanded Universe authors. Despite this, however, Lucas implied that the precepts of being a Jedi could be practiced by "anyone" when discussing the story treatment for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] in 1981 (then-titled ''Revenge of the Jedi''), and in particular the backstory for Anakin (who had been revealed to be Darth Vader), comparing it to yoga or karate.<ref name="The Making of Return of the Jedi">''[[The Making of Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]'', p. 62-69<br />
REVENGE OF THE JEDI STORY CONFERENCE TRANSCRIPT, JULY 13 to JULY 17, 1981—SUMMARY<br />
Participants: George Lucas, Richard Marquand, Lawrence Kasdan, and Howard Kazanjian<br />
Location: Park Way House<br />
''Note: Many of the ideas here are conceptual only and should not be considered as canon in the Star Wars saga.''<br />
[...]<br />
THE STORY OF ANAKIN<br />
'''Lawrence Kasadan:''' The Force was available to anyone who could hook into it?<br />
'''George Lucas:''' Yes, everyone can do it.<br />
'''Kasadan:''' Not just the Jedi?<br />
'''Lucas:''' It's just the Jedi who take the time to do it.<br />
'''Marquand:''' They use it as a technique.<br />
'''Lucas:''' Like yoga. If you want to take the time to do it, you can do it; but the ones that really want to do it are the ones who are into that kind of thing. Also like karate.</ref> In addition, JW Rinzler also indicated in another interview that George Lucas added the midi-chlorian concept to his statements after the fact in the ''Making of Star Wars'' hardcover edition.<ref name="SW-So What the Heck Are Midi-Chlorians?">{{SW|url=news/so-what-the-heck-are-midi-chlorians|text=So What the Heck Are Midi-Chlorians?}}</ref>

[[File:Mitochondrion.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A mitochondrion, inspiration for the midi-chlorians]]
Midi-chlorians in ''The Phantom Menace'' are part of a recurring theme throughout the movie, that of symbiotic relationships.<ref name="TPM DVD" /> They were loosely based on [[Wikipedia:Mitochondrion|mitochondria]], organelles that provide energy for cells; like midi-chlorians, mitochondria are believed to have once been separate organisms that inhabited living cells and have since become part of them; even now, mitochondria act in some ways as independent lifeforms, with DNA all their own. Lucas established this relation with mitochondria, in particular the necessity of midi-chlorians for life to exist, as a metaphor for society; namely, he says all parts of society must get along in much the same way the midi-chlorians and their symbiont do.<ref name="TFN1">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/midichlorians/midi-what.asp|text=What are Midi-Chlorians?|work=[[TheForce.net|TheForce.Net]]|archivedate=20050218100344}}</ref> In [[2006]]&mdash;as a tribute to this similarity&mdash;a newly discovered species of bacteria residing within mitochondria was named [[Wikipedia:Midichloria|''Midichloria mitochondrii'']] after the midi-chlorians. Its discoverer, Nate Lo, wrote to Lucas requesting permission to use the name, and was granted it.<ref name="Bacteria">{{WebCite|url=http://www.the-scientist.com/article/home/36660|text=Use the force, bacteria|author=Stepehen Pincock|date=2006-12-01|work=[[Wikipedia:The Scientist (magazine)|''The Scientist'']]|archivedate=20070108185802|nolive=1}}</ref>

Though midi-chlorians would not make a public appearance until 1999, pre&ndash;''Phantom Menace'' Expanded Universe materials hinted at an individual's biological connection to the Force. In ''[[Jedi Search]]'', [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] carries out a search for potential Jedi for Luke Skywalker's new [[Jedi Praxeum|academy]] by using a device that can detect affinity to the Force. In the [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|''Thrawn Trilogy'']], two organisms are mentioned, the [[vornskr]]s and the [[Ysalamiri/Legends|ysalamiri]], that have evolved the ability respectively to use the Force to hunt prey and block the Force.{{Quote|Back in the day, I used to say ultimately what this means is we were just cars, vehicles, for the Whills to travel around in.... We're vessels for them. And the conduit is the midi-chlorians. The midi-chlorians are the ones who communicate with The Whills. The Whills, in a general sense, they are the Force.|[[George Lucas]], in "James Cameron's Story of Science Fiction"|<ref name="James Cameron">{{Amazon|url=James-Camerons-Story-Science-Fiction/dp/1683834976|text=James Cameron's Story of Science Fiction}}</ref>}}Back in 2018, [[George Lucas]], in "James Cameron's Story of Science Fiction" stated that The Midi-chlorians were conduits used by cars (ourselves) that carried passengers ([[Ancient Order of the Whills|Whills]]) to travel around in, explaining later that The Midi-chlorians communicate with those passengers.

===Non-canonical information===
[[File:Midi-chlorians.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The midi-chlorians, according to ''Star Wars Tales 10'']]
On [[April 1]], 2006, several entries relating to George Lucas' [[Willow (film)|''Willow'']] universe were added to the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] as an [[Wikipedia:April Fools' Day|April Fools' Day]] joke. The update page names the planet [[Andowyne]] as the possible homeworld of the midi-chlorians.<ref name="Shadow">{{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/401/news20060401.html|text=The Shadow War Chronicles}}</ref>

The non-canonical comic ''[[Tag & Bink: Revenge of the Clone Menace]]'' tells of other effects of Darth Plagueis' manipulations of the midi-chlorians: [[Tag Greenly|Tag Greenley]] and [[Bink Otauna/Legends|Bink Otauna]] became Force-sensitive, while a red [[Star/Legends|sun]] and its planet, whose only survivor would go on to become a hero on Earth, was destroyed&mdash;references to [[Wikipedia:Krypton (comics)|Krypton]] and [[Wikipedia:Superman|Superman]], respectively.

In the introduction page to [[Star Wars Tales 10|''Star Wars Tales'' 10]], [[Dark Horse Comics]] editor [[David Land]] goes inside a Jedi Knight with the help of [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[2-1B/Legends|2-1B]] in search of midi-chlorians. He finds they look like assistant editor [[Philip Simon]], then orders them back to work.

The ''Tales'' story "[[Skippy the Jedi Droid]]" mentions the similarly-named [[midi-chloroxian]]s, found in the [[Lubricant/Legends|lubricants]] of [[R5-D4/Legends|the eponymous droid]], which gave it mastery of the Force.

===Controversy===
Midi-chlorians have had some negative reception among fans; some see them as adding hard science to the alleged "mysteriousness" or spirituality of the Force and dislike what they see as a new concept. Others, however, believe that having a physical aspect to a mystical Force calls upon real-world religious traditions, feeling that the mythic qualities of the Force have been strengthened by midi-chlorians.

A misconception exists that rather than being indicators, midi-chlorians actually ''are'' the Force or create it; there is no canonical basis for this belief.<ref name="TFN2">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/midichlorians/index.asp|text=Midi-Chlorians: Physiology, Physics, and the Force|work=[[TheForce.net|TheForce.Net]]|archivedate=20050218100245}}</ref><ref name="Blogspot">{{Blogspot|subdomain=sciencefictionbiology|url=2007/06/star-wars-and-midi-chlorian-menace.html|name=Biology in Science Fiction|text=Star Wars and the Midi-Chlorian Menace}}</ref><ref name="Metafilter">{{WebCite|url=http://www.metafilter.com/68999/Star-Wars-The-Clone-Wars|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars|work=Metafilter|archivedate=20090219001609}}</ref> [[Steve Perry]], who used midi-chlorians in his novel [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']], opined that they were "less than inspired."<ref name="Perry">{{WebCite|url=http://yildizsavaslari.com/inceleme/steveperry/index_eng.html|text=Steve Perry Interview|work=[http://yildizsavaslari.com YILDIZSAVSLARI.COM]|archivedate=20130213161856}}</ref> George Lucas, on the other hand, considers the two aspects of the Force separately, treating the midi-chlorians as the practical, biological side, distinct from the spiritual and metaphysical side of the Force.<ref name="TPM DVD" />
